title: Regulation of Ownership of Personal Mobility Aids to Prevent Their Misuse and Abuse
what_it_is: Regulation of Ownership of Personal Mobility Aids to Prevent Their Misuse and Abuse

sections.label: PMA safety rules and enforcement
sections.summary: LTA regulates PMA safety, not ownership, with a 10 km/h speed limit and penalties for non-compliant devices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Rather than regulate ownership, LTA has regulations to ensure that PMAs are safe for use on public paths.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: All PMAs, which include mobility scooters and motorised wheelchairs, have a maximum speed of 10 kilometres per hour (km/h) and mobility scooters must only have a single seat, among other requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: LTA conducts regular enforcement efforts islandwide and users found to be using non-compliant devices may face a fine of up to $10,000 and imprisonment of up to six months, and also have their devices impounded.

sections.label: Review of PMA rules
sections.summary: The Active Mobility Advisory Panel's workplan includes reviewing PMA rules and restrictions, such as pre-conditions for use.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: As part of the workplan of the Active Mobility Advisory Panel, which started its new term in January 2022, there will be a review of the rules and restrictions applicable to PMAs, such as setting pre-conditions for a person to use PMAs.

sections.label: Public reports and enforcement hotspots
sections.summary: LTA collates public reports to identify hotspot areas for stepped-up enforcement, though immediate deployment is not possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: When members of the public report such cases, it could be through a video, a photograph or just information about the incident via the MyTransport.SG app.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: LTA will collate the information based on the locations where these errant users are or non-compliant devices are used.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: LTA will identify these hotspot areas  where they will step up enforcement actions on the ground.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: I hope for Members and public's understanding that LTA will not be able to deploy and enforce immediately because, by the time they reach the spots, the riders would already not be there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: But the information is very useful for us to know which are the hotspot areas so that more enforcement could be deployed there.
